A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a low-power receiver circuit with a compact layout, which can be used in source-synchronous link configurations.
we have developed a receiver circuit for source-synchronous links that is optimized for low-power operation and is suitable for high-speed operation up to 12.5 GB/s in 32 nm technology.

we have shown that the power consumption of the transceiver can be reduced by using a link protocol which enables periodic calibration, by using a linear equalizer on the receive side only and by implementing the DFE using SC circuits.

the use of a SC-DFE and the avoidance of a TX-FFE can lead to a low-power receiver implementation, which is particularly beneficial for high-speed serial links in which the transmit circuit is already very complex and power hungry.
a source-synchronous receiver design can be optimized for power consumption and area, even when the link is not optimized for power.
